1"""In-place elementwise bitwise XOR (``A ^= B``) for Ascend NPU, written in TLE. 

2 

3Semantics of the reference (FlagGems ``bitwise_xor_tensor_``): every element of 

4``A`` is replaced by ``A[i] ^ B[i]`` and the **same tensor object** is returned, 

5so the caller observes ``out is A`` with ``A`` mutated in place. 

6 

7Kernel shape: **vec-explicit** (from the TLE shape decision tree -- the operator 

8has no ``tl.dot``, needs no cross-engine handshake and is pure streaming, so the 

9whole story is explicit UB staging): 

10 

11 GM -> (MTE2, ``tle.dsa.copy``) -> UB -> ``triton.language`` ``^`` -> GM 

12 

13XOR has no member in the TLE elementwise set, so the compute itself is plain 

14``triton.language``, as the implementation profile requires; every eligible bulk 

15tile move goes through ``tle.dsa.copy``. 

16 

17Two launches, and why the staged kernel has no branch 

18----------------------------------------------------- 

19``tle.dsa.copy`` takes an explicit shape but **no mask**, so a tensor whose 

20length is not a multiple of the tile width needs a masked tail. Round 3 kept 

21that tail *inside* the staged kernel as an ``if base + BLOCK <= n: ... else: 

22...`` branch, and the round-3 compiler IR showed the price: the compiler 

23allocated UB for the buffers of *both* sides of the branch and applied its 

24automatic double buffering (``hivm.multi_buffer = 2``) to all six of them, for an 

25180224-byte claim inside the 192 KB UB -- including the three buffers that belong 

26only to the masked side, which is entered at most once per program and never at 

27all in any measured timing shape. 

28 

29So the ragged remainder is handled by a **separate masked kernel** launched over 

30``n_full .. n``, and the staged kernel is branch-free: it is launched only over 

31the full-tile prefix ``n_full = (n // block) * block`` and its body carries no 

32conditional and no mask. Inputs shorter than ``_SMALL_LIMIT`` skip the staged 

33kernel entirely and go straight to the masked kernel, which is what keeps the 

3464x64 cases (4096 elements) off a wide mask. Measured effect of the split at an 

35unchanged 16384-byte payload: the double buffering is retained and the L2-resident 

36latencies reproduce the branch-carrying round-3 form to within 0.6%, so the 

37branch removal is free; the 2**30 cells come out 1.7% (bool) and 0.2% (int16) 

38faster than round 3. 

39 

40Why the tile is sized in bytes and not in elements 

41-------------------------------------------------- 

42Round-1 profiling (msprof, CANN 9.0.0) showed the kernel losing on the narrow 

43element types with MTE2 as the busiest pipe (duty ~0.905 at 2**30) while VEC sat 

44at 0.16-0.19, so the GM->UB staging path -- not the vector op -- sets the cost. 

45Round-3 profiling confirmed that ordering on the then-current source (MTE2 duty 

460.87-0.90 against VEC 0.17-0.19 and MTE3 0.21-0.42) and added the decisive fact: 

47a larger staged payload still pays even at constant total bytes. Going from a 

484 KB to a 16 KB payload at an unchanged byte count cut the 2**30 bool case from 

494.636087 to 2.878829 ms (-38%) and the 2**30 int16 case from 6.483386 to 

505.702362 ms (-12%), while int32 -- whose payload was already 16 KB and therefore 

51did not change -- stayed flat. A pure bandwidth wall forbids that, so a 

52copy-count-dependent term of the form ``t = bytes/W + copies*F`` with 

53``F ~ 0.04-0.06 us`` per staged copy was still being paid at 16 KB. 

54 

55The tile is therefore chosen from a *payload byte* target: each of the two staged 

56GM->UB copies moves ~``payload`` bytes. Round 2 introduced the byte target but an 

57element clamp truncated it (uint8 4 KB, int16 8 KB); round 3 lifted that and 

58reached 16 KB at every width; round 4 doubled it to 32 KB. 

59 

60Why the payload is dispatched on L2 residency 

61--------------------------------------------- 

62The payload cannot be one constant, because the two workload regimes want 

63opposite things, and the round-4/round-5 pair isolates the reason. 

64 

65The compiler's live UB set is three buffers: the two staging buffers plus the 

66value ``tl.store`` needs (the UB->GM direction of ``tle.dsa.copy`` does not lower 

67on this toolchain -- see below). At a 16384-byte payload that is 

68``3 x 2 x 16384 = 98304 B`` of the 192 KB per-core UB with the automatic double 

69buffering retained -- three ``hivm.multi_buffer = 2`` marks, no UB-overflow note 

70(round 5, confirmed from the captured NPUIR). At 32768 bytes the doubled 

71footprint would be 196608 B, so the compiler reports ``[NOTE] Ub overflow 

72detected; automatically set enable-auto-multi-buffer to false`` and drops the 

73marks entirely (round 4). The UB budget, not the claim size, is binding: both 

74payloads claim 98304 B, one double buffered and one not. 

75 

76Which of the two is faster depends on whether the copies wait on DRAM. 

77 

78 * Footprint not in L2 (the two 2**30 shapes, and the int32 2**24 case at 

79 192 MiB > 168 MiB): the copies wait on DRAM, so the MTE2/VEC overlap is what 

80 keeps MTE2 busy -- at 2**30 it is genuinely bandwidth-ceilinged, MTE2 duty 

81 0.8905 at a uniform ~1.13 TB/s for every width. The 16384-byte 

82 multi-buffered payload wins there (bool::0 2.831153 against round 4's 

83 2.821451 -- inside the per-cell noise floor -- and int32::2/::3 0.175745 / 

84 0.176071 against round 4's 0.1871, i.e. 6%). 

85 * Footprint in L2 (bool and int16 at 2**24: 48 MiB and 96 MiB of 168 MiB): no 

86 pipe is saturated (round-5 profile: MTE2 0.5672/0.5943, VEC only marginally 

87 higher at 0.6056/0.6316, MTE3 ~0.44), so these cells are limited by per-copy 

88 overhead and dependency serialization, and there the 32768-byte payload -- 

89 half the iterations per program -- is 8.6-12.3% faster (bool::2/::3 

90 0.012716/0.012705, int16::2/::3 0.022337/0.022238, against 0.013915/0.013919 

91 and 0.025445/0.025440 at 16384 B). 

92 

93So the payload is selected at run time from ``3 * n * itemsize <= L2``: the wide 

94payload for a footprint the cache can hold, the narrow multi-buffered one 

95otherwise. ``int32`` at 2**24 makes the rule self-consistent -- at 192 MiB it 

96misses the cache and indeed prefers the narrow payload, exactly like the 2**30 

97cells. The L2 capacity is read from the live device and never hard-coded: the 

98submission target is Ascend910B2, which need not be the SKU the development 

99service reports, and a failed query simply keeps the narrow payload. 

100 

101Why the write-back is ``tl.store`` and not ``tle.dsa.copy`` 

102----------------------------------------------------------- 

103On this toolchain (CANN 9.0.0, FlagTree ascend3.5 line) the UB->GM direction of 

104``tle.dsa.copy`` does not lower: 

105 

106 * source is a register tensor -> the TileIR ``tile.copy`` becomes a 

107 ``hivm.hir`` load of the output, rejected by BiShengIR 

108 (``hivm.hir.load op only support src == gm and dst != gm``); 

109 * source is a UB buffer -> ``TritonToLinalgIncubated`` dies with 

110 ``failed to legalize unresolved materialization from 

111 ('memref<1xi16, strided<[1], offset: ?>>') to ('!tt.ptr<i16>')``. 

112 

113Routing the result back into ``a_ub`` so the store reads a *buffer* does not 

114avoid it either: both ``tle.dsa.to_buffer`` and a tensor->buffer ``tle.dsa.copy`` 

115fail in the same ``TritonToLinalgIncubated`` pass (probe V0-V3), and 

116``tle.dsa.insert_slice`` is defined over tensors, not buffers. The GM->UB 

117direction does have a legal form: a ``tl.make_block_ptr`` source (the pointer is 

118materialised inside the block pointer rather than as a bare ``tt.addptr``), which 

119is what this kernel uses. ``tl.store`` is therefore the documented escape hatch 

120for the one access DSA cannot express, and it is the only non-DSA movement in the 

121kernel -- at the cost of the third live UB value that bounds the payload above. 

122 

123Why one kernel per element count and not one per shape 

124------------------------------------------------------ 

125The op is bit granular: XOR is independent per bit, so the payload can be staged 

126under any same-width integer type without changing a single output bit. The 

127kernel is written against ``element_ty`` and stages whatever type the pointers 

128carry, which keeps ``int16``/``int32`` on native vector lanes. ``torch.bool`` 

129is the single exception -- Triton models it as ``i1``, which has no UB buffer 

130form -- so the wrapper hands the kernel a zero-copy ``uint8`` view (one byte per 

131element, 0/1 valued, so byte-wise XOR is exactly the logical XOR). 

132 

133This is *not* expressed with ``@triton.autotune``: this operator mutates ``A`` in 

134place and XOR is not idempotent, so a tuner that benchmarks a configuration by 

135re-launching the kernel would XOR ``A`` with ``B`` once per benchmarking 

136repetition and corrupt the very result the harness checks afterwards. The tile 

137is therefore a deterministic host-side dispatch on ``(n, element size, L2)``. 

138 

139Grid and portability 

140-------------------- 

141The submission target is Ascend910B2 while the development/evaluation service 

142may report a different 910B SKU, so both the core count and the L2 capacity are 

143queried from the live device at run time and never hard-coded; the grid is capped 

144both by that core count and by the device's 1-D grid limit, and the tiles a 

145program cannot reach in one pass are picked up by an interleaved strided loop 

146(``pid``, ``pid + nprog``, ...). This is what keeps the 2**30-element cases 

147legal: their tile count exceeds the maximum 1-D grid extent, so a 

148single-tile-per-program launch could not cover them. 

149""" 

150 

151from __future__ import annotations 

152 

153import logging 

154 

155import torch 

156import torch_npu # noqa: F401 (must precede triton on this stack) 

157import triton 

158import triton.experimental.tle as tle 

159import triton.language as tl 

160 

161logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

162 

163# Bytes moved by one staged GM->UB copy. The per-copy fixed cost of 

164# ``tle.dsa.copy`` (~0.04-0.06 us measured at 2**30) is amortised over this many 

165# bytes, and it is also the UB budget knob: the compiler's live UB set is three 

166# buffers, so ``3 x 2 x payload`` must fit the per-core UB for the automatic 

167# double buffering (``hivm.multi_buffer = 2``) to survive. 

168# 

169# * _PAYLOAD_WIDE = 32768 -> ``3 x 32768 = 98304 B`` single buffered after the 

170# compiler reports "Ub overflow detected". Measured 8.6-12.3% faster on the 

171# cells whose footprint fits L2, where the copies do not wait on DRAM and the 

172# halved iteration count is what counts. 

173# * _PAYLOAD_NARROW = 16384 -> ``3 x 2 x 16384 = 98304 B`` with double 

174# buffering retained (three ``hivm.multi_buffer = 2`` marks, no overflow 

175# note). The choice whenever the footprint misses the cache, where the 

176# MTE2/VEC overlap is what keeps the bandwidth-bound stream busy. 

177_PAYLOAD_NARROW = 16384 

178_PAYLOAD_WIDE = 32768 

179 

180# Smallest tile tolerated, so short tensors still get a usable vector width. 

181_BLOCK_MIN = 1024 

182 

183# Largest tile tolerated, i.e. the wide payload divided by the narrowest element 

184# (uint8). Round 2 measured the fixed per-copy staging term on top of a ~16 KB 

185# payload: at a 4096-element clamp the uint8 copy moved only 4 KB and the int16 

186# copy 8 KB, so the byte target was not reached and those two types still lost. 

187# At the wide payload every width stages its full payload (uint8 32768, int16 

188# 16384, int32 8192 elements); at the narrow payload the clamp is not reached at 

189# all (uint8 16384 elements exactly). 

190_BLOCK_MAX = 32768 

191 

192# Element counts at or below this are dominated by launch cost and are too small 

193# to fill a wide tile, so they go straight to the masked kernel with the narrow 

194# proven tile rather than paying a wide mask over a fraction of the work: a wide 

195# tile over a tiny tensor would push the whole problem through the masked path, 

196# paying a full wide mask and a wide UB allocation for a fraction of the work 

197# (measured as 0.708x for a 4096-element int32 tensor in the sibling out-of-place 

198# operator, which is why that dispatch exists there too). 

199_SMALL_LIMIT = 8192 

200_BLOCK_SMALL = 2048 

201 

202# Ascend allows at most 65535 programs per grid dimension; used only when the 

203# live vector-core count cannot be read. 

204_MAX_GRID_1D = 65535 

205 

206# Programs wanted per vector core. A small multiple keeps several independent 

207# MTE2/MTE3 streams in flight per core without letting the grid run away on the 

208# large shapes. 

209_PROGRAMS_PER_CORE = 8 

210 

211_NUM_VEC_CORES = None 

212_L2_BYTES = {} 

213 

214 

215def _num_vector_cores(): 

216 """Live vector-core count of the *actual* target device (0 when unknown). 

217 

218 Never hard-code a core count observed on the development device: the 

219 submission target is Ascend910B2, which need not be the SKU the service 

220 reports. This is output-independent target state, so it is resolved once and 

221 reused; when the target will not report it the caller falls back to the 

222 device's maximum 1-D grid extent. 

223 """ 

224 global _NUM_VEC_CORES 

225 if _NUM_VEC_CORES is not None: 

226 return _NUM_VEC_CORES 

227 

228 count = 0 

229 try: 

230 from triton.backends.ascend import driver as _ascend_driver 

231 

232 props = _ascend_driver.active.utils.get_device_properties( 

233 torch.npu.current_device() 

234 ) 

235 if isinstance(props, dict): 

236 count = props.get("num_vectorcore") or props.get("vector_core_num") or 0 

237 else: 

238 count = getattr(props, "num_vectorcore", 0) or getattr( 

239 props, "vector_core_num", 0 

240 ) 

241 except Exception: 

242 count = 0 

243 

244 if not count: 

245 try: 

246 count = int( 

247 torch.npu.get_device_properties( 

248 torch.npu.current_device() 

249 ).vector_core_num 

250 ) 

251 except Exception: 

252 count = 0 

253 

254 _NUM_VEC_CORES = int(count) if count else 0 

255 return _NUM_VEC_CORES 

256 

257 

258def _l2_bytes(device_index): 

259 """L2 capacity of the live device, or 0 when it cannot be read. 

260 

261 Same portability rule as the core count: read it, never assume it. On this 

262 stack the Triton Ascend driver exposes no ``active`` handle at all, so the 

263 query goes through ``torch.npu``, whose ``_NPUDeviceProperties`` carries 

264 ``L2_cache_size``. A failed query returns 0, which selects the narrow 

265 payload for every shape -- always correct, just not specialised. 

266 """ 

267 idx = int(device_index) 

268 if idx in _L2_BYTES: 

269 return _L2_BYTES[idx] 

270 

271 value = 0 

272 try: 

273 props = torch.npu.get_device_properties(idx) 

274 value = int(getattr(props, "L2_cache_size", 0) or 0) 

275 except Exception: 

276 value = 0 

277 

278 _L2_BYTES[idx] = value 

279 return value 

280 

281 

282def _pick_block(n, itemsize, l2_bytes): 

283 """Tile width in elements for ``n`` elements of ``itemsize`` bytes. 

284 

285 ``l2_bytes`` is the live device L2 capacity (0 when unknown). The in-place 

286 operator reads ``A``, reads ``B`` and writes ``A``, so its streaming footprint 

287 is ``3 * n * itemsize`` bytes; the wide payload is chosen only when that whole 

288 footprint fits the cache, i.e. only when the staged copies do not have to wait 

289 on DRAM. Dispatch is deterministic on ``(n, itemsize, l2)`` by design -- see 

290 the module docstring on why an autotuner cannot be used here. 

291 """ 

292 payload = _PAYLOAD_NARROW 

293 if l2_bytes and 3 * n * itemsize <= l2_bytes: 

294 payload = _PAYLOAD_WIDE 

295 

296 block = payload // itemsize 

297 if block < _BLOCK_MIN: 

298 block = _BLOCK_MIN 

299 if block > _BLOCK_MAX: 

300 block = _BLOCK_MAX 

301 return block 

302 

303 

304def _grid_for(ntile): 

305 """Program count for ``ntile`` tiles, capped by the live vector-core count. 

306 

307 The tiles a program cannot reach in one pass are picked up by the kernel's 

308 interleaved strided loop, so capping the grid is safe at any tensor size; the 

309 cap only exists to keep the 2**30-element cases inside the 1-D grid extent 

310 and to avoid oversubscribing the cores. 

311 """ 

312 cap = _num_vector_cores() * _PROGRAMS_PER_CORE or _MAX_GRID_1D 

313 return (ntile if ntile < cap else cap,) 

314 

315 

316@triton.jit 

317def _bitwise_xor_inplace_kernel(a_ptr, b_ptr, o_ptr, n, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): 

318 """``o[i] = a[i] ^ b[i]`` for ``n`` elements, ``n`` a multiple of ``BLOCK``. 

319 

320 For the in-place operator ``o_ptr`` *is* ``a_ptr``: each tile is read into UB 

321 before anything is written back, and every program owns a disjoint set of 

322 tiles, so the update is race-free without any extra synchronisation. 

323 

324 The body is deliberately branch-free and mask-free, so the compiler's 

325 automatic double buffering applies to exactly the three buffers the loop 

326 really uses (see the module docstring); the caller guarantees 

327 ``n % BLOCK == 0`` and the ragged remainder is handled by 

328 ``_bitwise_xor_masked_kernel``. 

329 

330 Tiles are assigned to programs in an interleaved stride (``pid``, 

331 ``pid + nprog``, ...) so that the tiles being streamed at any instant lie in 

332 one contiguous region of the tensor. 

333 """ 

334 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

335 nprog = tl.num_programs(0) 

336 ntile = tl.cdiv(n, BLOCK) 

337 

338 # Allocated once, outside the loop: a ``tile.alloc`` must not sit inside a 

339 # conditional region, and one staging pair per program is reused by every 

340 # tile the program owns. 

341 a_ub = tle.dsa.alloc([BLOCK], a_ptr.dtype.element_ty, tle.dsa.ascend.UB) 

342 b_ub = tle.dsa.alloc([BLOCK], b_ptr.dtype.element_ty, tle.dsa.ascend.UB) 

343 

344 for tile in range(pid, ntile, nprog): 

345 base = tile * BLOCK 

346 a_bp = tl.make_block_ptr( 

347 a_ptr, 

348 shape=(n,), 

349 strides=(1,), 

350 offsets=(base,), 

351 block_shape=(BLOCK,), 

352 order=(0,), 

353 ) 

354 b_bp = tl.make_block_ptr( 

355 b_ptr, 

356 shape=(n,), 

357 strides=(1,), 

358 offsets=(base,), 

359 block_shape=(BLOCK,), 

360 order=(0,), 

361 ) 

362 tle.dsa.copy(a_bp, a_ub, [BLOCK]) 

363 tle.dsa.copy(b_bp, b_ub, [BLOCK]) 

364 tl.store( 

365 o_ptr + base + tl.arange(0, BLOCK), 

366 tle.dsa.to_tensor(a_ub) ^ tle.dsa.to_tensor(b_ub), 

367 ) 

368 

369 

370@triton.jit 

371def _bitwise_xor_masked_kernel(a_ptr, b_ptr, o_ptr, start, n, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): 

372 """Masked ``o[i] = a[i] ^ b[i]`` over ``[start, n)``. 

373 

374 Handles both the ragged remainder of a large tensor and, on its own, the 

375 whole of a small one. The ``_bitwise_xor_inplace_kernel``'s reason to 

376 exclude this work is UB budget, not correctness: ``tle.dsa.copy`` has no 

377 mask, so an unmasked tile cannot be issued near the end of a tensor. 

378 """ 

379 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

380 nprog = tl.num_programs(0) 

381 ntile = tl.cdiv(n - start, BLOCK) 

382 

383 for tile in range(pid, ntile, nprog): 

384 offs = start + tile * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

385 mask = offs < n 

386 x = tl.load(a_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0) 

387 y = tl.load(b_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0) 

388 tl.store(o_ptr + offs, x ^ y, mask=mask) 

389 

390 

391def _payload(t): 

392 """Zero-copy byte view for ``torch.bool``. 

393 

394 ``bool`` occupies one byte per element, so the 8-bit payload view preserves 

395 the bit patterns -- and therefore the XOR result -- while giving the UB 

396 buffers and the vector unit a plain 8-bit integer type to work on. 

397 """ 

398 if t.dtype == torch.bool: 

399 return t.view(torch.uint8) 

400 return t 

401 

402 

403_SUPPORTED_DTYPES = ( 

404 torch.bool, 

405 torch.uint8, 

406 torch.int8, 

407 torch.int16, 

408 torch.int32, 

409 torch.int64, 

410) 

411 

412 

413def bitwise_xor_tensor_(A, B, out0=None, *args, **kwargs): 

414 """``A ^= B`` in place; returns the mutated tensor.""" 

415 logger.debug("GEMS BITWISE_XOR_TENSOR_") 

416 if A.dtype not in _SUPPORTED_DTYPES: 

417 from flag_gems.ops.bitwise_xor import bitwise_xor_tensor_ as _generic 

418 

419 return _generic(A, B) 

420 

421 """``A ^= B`` in place (or ``out0 = A ^ B`` when ``out0`` is supplied). 

422 

423 Returns the mutated tensor object itself, so the declared reference call form 

424 ``bitwise_xor_tensor_(A, B)`` satisfies ``out is A``. 

425 

426 Only layout and metadata work happens on the host: the flattened views are 

427 zero-copy for dense inputs, and every numeric element is produced by the 

428 device kernels. When it can be expressed the fused form is always valid 

429 (``out0 is A`` makes ``o_ptr`` and ``a_ptr`` the same allocation), so the 

430 split into a full-tile launch plus a masked remainder launch is purely a 

431 kernel-shape decision, never a semantic one. 

432 """ 

433 target = A if out0 is None else out0 

434 

435 if A.numel() == 0: 

436 return target 

437 

438 a_flat = _payload(A).reshape(-1) 

439 b_flat = _payload(B).reshape(-1) 

440 o_flat = _payload(target).reshape(-1) 

441 n = a_flat.numel() 

442 

443 if n <= _SMALL_LIMIT: 

444 _bitwise_xor_masked_kernel[_grid_for(triton.cdiv(n, _BLOCK_SMALL))]( 

445 a_flat, b_flat, o_flat, 0, n, BLOCK=_BLOCK_SMALL 

446 ) 

447 return target 

448 

449 device_index = a_flat.device.index 

450 block = _pick_block( 

451 n, a_flat.element_size(), _l2_bytes(0 if device_index is None else device_index) 

452 ) 

453 n_full = (n // block) * block 

454 

455 if n_full: 

456 _bitwise_xor_inplace_kernel[_grid_for(n_full // block)]( 

457 a_flat, b_flat, o_flat, n_full, BLOCK=block 

458 ) 

459 if n_full < n: 

460 _bitwise_xor_masked_kernel[_grid_for(triton.cdiv(n - n_full, _BLOCK_SMALL))]( 

461 a_flat, b_flat, o_flat, n_full, n, BLOCK=_BLOCK_SMALL 

462 ) 

463 return target
